correctness.rationale: When \(T(M)\) is a submodule, the nonzero torsion vertices form \(K_{\alpha-1}\) and have no edges to nontorsion vertices. Nontorsion adjacency depends only on quotient cosets and pairs a coset with its negative. If \(2\in Z(R)\), every quotient coset equals its negative and each nonzero coset induces \(K_\alpha\); if \(2\notin Z(R)\), nonzero cosets pair into \(K_{\alpha,\alpha}\) components. Therefore isolated vertices occur exactly for \(\alpha=2\), or for \(\alpha=1\) with \(2\in Z(R)\). Every other nontrivial component has total and paired domination number two, so summing componentwise gives the three displayed formulas. The bundled exact checker realizes all boundary regimes over small \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) examples and checks bounded abstract parameter profiles; the arbitrary finite-module theorem rests on the coset proof.
residual_risks: The theorem requires finite \(M\) and additive closure of \(T(M)\).
